statement: For regular smooth real canonical genus-four sextics, the possible numbers of real tritangent planes are exactly 0, 8, 16, 24, 32, 64, and 120.

source.location: Section 4.1 and Table 1, printed pp.6,8; real-plane classification attributed there to Gross–Harris

notes:
Here real means the plane is defined over R; its three contact points may include a conjugate pair. The table separately records totally-real contact counts, which can include odd numbers and are not this answer. The topology rows are respectively: no real components; 1 nondividing; 2 nondividing; 3 dividing; 3 nondividing; 4 nondividing; 5 dividing.

The underlying real odd-theta count is Gross–Harris, Proposition 5.1. Hauenstein et al. explicitly attribute their Table 1 to this theory; their new certification method is not the origin of the spectrum recorded here.
scope: Smooth nonhyperelliptic canonical curves of genus four with a regular odd-theta tritangent fibre.
